purpose: Define the DWH peer transport security envelope as session-scoped protection layered over WebRTC transport, separated from semantic authorization and data ownership.

topics.name: DWH Transport Security
topics.purpose: Define the DWH peer transport security envelope as session-scoped protection layered over WebRTC transport, separated from semantic authorization and data ownership.

semantics.session_protection: PGP/session-key based envelope according to the owning DWH transport security profile
semantics.handshake_marker: MD5 handshake marker where retained by the current DWH protocol profile
semantics.handshake_rule: Handshake/session verification establishes transport-session continuity only; it does not grant semantic authorization.
semantics.identity_rule: Peer semantic identity must still resolve explicitly outside the cryptographic/session handle.
semantics.payload_rule: Protected payload remains inert until DWH semantic/schema/origin validation.
semantics.key_state_rule: Session key/security context is runtime state with bounded lifetime and explicit cleanup.
semantics.separation_rule: Transport confidentiality/integrity/session continuity are separate from AccessCore authorization and DWH data policy.

invariants.rule: DWH local/remote, origin, schema, external identity, access path and transport-security semantics remain explicit and non-interchangeable.

hard_gates.condition: session/crypto handle becomes peer semantic identity
session key/security state persisted as canonical definition
transport protection substituted for AccessCore/DWH authorization

references.purpose: Security envelope rides on WebRTC P2P transport.
Payload transport remains separate from DWH semantics.
Session key/security context is runtime state.

prose.summary: Define the DWH peer transport security envelope as session-scoped protection layered over WebRTC transport, separated from semantic authorization and data ownership.
